Double-elimination |prizepoolusd=1,000,000 |liquipediatier=1 |leagueid=16518 |website=https://www.esl-one.com/birmingham/ |facebook=ESLDota2 |instagram=esldota2 |twitch=esl_dota2 |twitter=ESLDota2 |youtube=ESLDota2 |bracket=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lBSkUVz2JLk6tf1t8USx0ciGX9XYz1vtkj1oiF7C8j4/edit#gid=1608117644 |rulebook=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xTw9urVnsnVqePg_F46M6drprR8vK_Sz/view |headtohead=true |previous=ESL One/Kuala Lumpur/2023{{!}}Kuala Lumpur 2023 |previous2=DreamLeague/Season 22{{!}}DreamLeague Season 22 |next=ESL One/Bangkok/2024{{!}}Bangkok 2024 |next2=DreamLeague/Season 23{{!}}DreamLeague Season 23 }}{{#vardefine:headtohead|true}} '''ESL One Birmingham 2024''' was a tournament held in Birmingham, United Kingdom in April 2024. It marked the return of ESL One to Birmingham, who last hosted the event in [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2019|2019]]. The tournament began competitively, with no clear favourite. Team Falcons, however, gained momentum the quickest, and they beat [[BetBoom Team]] 3-0 in an ill-tempered Grand Final. The qualification process of ESL One Birmingham 2024 saw difficulties. Several players from Russia and Belarus were unable to obtain visas to enter the United Kingdom. The team most affected by this was [[1win]]. Despite deadline extensions, [[#1win visa issues and OG invite controversy|ESL eventually removed them from the event]], and sought a replacement, eventually settling on [[OG]]. This choice was controversial, as this deprived Eastern Europe of a team, but also allowed OG an opportunity to qualify for [[Riyadh Masters/2024|Riyadh Masters 2024]]. The event proved to be highly-successful for ESL. Esports Charts reported that the event broke several viewership records for any ESL One event, and reached mainstream coverage from the BBC and Sky News. {{Quote|There is just not one weak point in this team. Every single one of them — [[skiter]], [[Malr1ne]], [[ATF|Ammar]], [[Cr1t-]], [[Sneyking]] — just on top of the world. And we've seen them do it in previous tournaments, coming in and giving a 3-0 smackdown, and doing it here, in front of this fantastic crowd live in Birmingham — this has got to feel fantastic for them.|[[ODPixel]] after Team Falcons won the tournament|source={{cite web|url=https://www.twitch.tv/esl_dota2/clip/SoftGoodNeanderthalDancingBaby-dDKhxWqmQrFYjHQN|title=ODPixel on Team Falcons|author=ESL|date=2024-04-28}}}}

Double-elimination |sdate=2024-09-04 |edate=2024-09-15 |sort_date=2024-09-20 |prizepoolusd={{:The International/2024/prizepool}} |liquipediatier=1 |publishertier=international |leagueid=16935 |website=https://www.dota2.com/esports/ti13 |facebook=dota2 |instagram=dota2 |twitch=dota2ti |twitter=dota2ti |weibo=dota2comcn |youtube=dota2 |bracket=https://www.dota2.com/esports/ti13/schedule |rulebook=https://www.dota2.com/esports/ti13/tirules |headtohead=true |previous={{BASEPAGENAME}}/2023{{!}}2023 |next={{BASEPAGENAME}}/2025{{!}}2025 }}{{TOClimit|7}} '''The International 2024''' (also commonly called '''TI 2024''' or '''TI 13''') was the thirteenth annual edition of [[The International]] which took place in Copenhagen, Denmark. Similar to previous year, The International 2024 was split into two distinct phases: The qualifiers, group stage and playoffs (until top 8) were branded as part of ''The Road to The International'', while the playoffs for the remaining 8 teams were branded as ''The International'' itself. It was also the first edition of the tournament since [[The_International/2017|2017]] to select one or more participating teams through a direct invite process, and the first since [[The_International/2019|2019]] to feature open qualifiers.{{cite web|url=https://www.dota2.com/newsentry/4150708537258201339|title=The International 2024 - Direct Invites and The Road to TI|publisher=Valve|date=2024-05-27}}
